s1.syndrome_frame: Acute limb ischemia with aneurysm and hematoma
salient_findings: Swollen right knee and thigh with extensive bruising
Pulsatile mass extending into the mid-thigh
key_facts: 96-year-old man with benign prostatic disease and dementia
Presented after a collapse at home
Normocytic anemia (hemoglobin 119 g/L) on admission
D-dimer of 1095 ng/mL on admission
Neutrophilia (10.44 × 10^9/L) on admission
Initial diagnosis of venous thromboembolism was excluded
Discharged with antibiotics for a presumed urinary tract infection
Returned with a swollen right knee and thigh and extensive bruising
Lower limb ultrasound showed a patent venous system
45 mm popliteal artery aneurysm with an 11.4 × 5.2 cm medial leg hematoma
Worsening right-leg pain and difficulty walking on subsequent admission
Extensive bruising behind the right knee and posterior-medial thigh
Pulseless right foot without signs of acute ischemia
Repeat hemoglobin was 77 g/L
Computed tomography angiography demonstrated a 4 × 5 cm saccular popliteal artery aneurysm

shortlist.label: Popliteal artery aneurysm
shortlist.why_kept: Confirmed by computed tomography angiography and lower limb ultrasound

shortlist.label: Arterial thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Pulseless right foot and extensive bruising suggest thrombotic complication

shortlist.label: Atherosclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Severely diseased runoff vessels and patient's age suggest atherosclerotic disease

shortlist.label: Thromboangiitis obliterans
shortlist.why_kept: Younger age not typical, but possible given complex presentation and aneurysm

shortlist.label: Pseudoaneurysm
shortlist.why_kept: Possible complication of popliteal artery aneurysm, given clinical presentation

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a swollen right knee and thigh, extensive bruising, and subsequent imaging findings of a 45 mm popliteal artery aneurysm with a large hematoma, as well as computed tomography angiography demonstrating a 4 × 5 cm saccular popliteal artery aneurysm, strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Arterial thrombosis
rejected.why: While the patient had a pulseless right foot, the absence of signs of acute ischemia and the presence of a large aneurysm with hematoma suggest that thrombosis is not the primary issue.

rejected.label: Atherosclerosis
rejected.why: Although the patient's runoff vessels were severely diseased, this is not the primary diagnosis that explains the patient's acute presentation and imaging findings.

rejected.label: Thromboangiitis obliterans
rejected.why: This condition typically affects younger patients and is characterized by inflammation and thrombosis of small and medium-sized arteries, which does not match the patient's presentation or imaging findings.

rejected.label: Pseudoaneurysm
rejected.why: The imaging findings describe a saccular popliteal artery aneurysm, which is a true aneurysm, rather than a pseudoaneurysm, which is a false aneurysm that occurs due to a disruption of the arterial wall.
